newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-WMC sees gold price slump short term.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-WMC sees gold price slump short term.

text.p: The managing director of metals miner WMC Ltd, Hugh Morgan, said on Wednesday the recent slump in the gold price was not unusual after a long period of relative stability and should be a short term move.

"What we've seen is that the gold price has been remarkably stable when you compare it with other commodities," Morgan told Reuters after chairing a mining seminar at the National Trade and Investment Outlook Conference.
"It's not unusual from time to time to see it move outside what was thought to be the accepted band of say US$380 an ounce to US$400," Morgan said.
"It seems as if the band may have increased somewhat for a short period of time," he said.
Morgan would not make any specific comment on how the slump might affect WMC's earnings.
"For those who have been in the gold mining industry for a long time nothing should be regarded as being unusual."
Morgan, who is a member of the board of the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA), said he would not comment on the recent rise in the Australian dollar or its sharp fall on Tuesday night.
The RBA board met on Tuesday and on Tuesday evening former governor Bernie Fraser said he would have cut official interest rates by further than the incumbent Ian Macfarlane.
The comment triggered a sharp fall by the Australian dollar overnight.
